title: Remote Work Policy
body:
Remote Work Policy
Owner: Catherine Hale, Chief Executive Officer
Last updated: 2026-07-30

Purpose and Scope
This policy sets out when and how Halcyon Ridge Capital employees may work away from the New York office. It applies to all staff in the Executive Office, Trading, Wealth Management, Lending, M&A Advisory, Compliance, Risk, Operations, and Technology. Flexibility is a privilege that depends on protecting client information, meeting regulatory obligations, and keeping critical systems supervised.

Eligibility and Schedules
Most roles may work remotely up to two days per week, agreed with your department head and recorded in HRIS. Teams must keep core in-office coverage on each business day. Trading, the Wire Room, and Settlements need on-site staffing during market hours and the daily cutoff windows. Employees in their first 60 days should work on-site unless their department head approves otherwise.

Access and Security Requirements
All remote access goes through AuthSSO with multi-factor authentication. Work only on firm-issued laptops with disk encryption and the managed endpoint agent installed. Connect through the corporate VPN whenever you access internal systems. Personal devices may not be used to download, store, or forward firm data. Do not use public Wi-Fi without VPN, and lock your screen whenever you step away. Documents belong in DocVault, never in personal cloud storage, personal email, or consumer messaging apps. Do not print firm or client material at home.

Team-Specific Rules
Trading: Traders on the desk may not run OMS or TradeBlotter sessions from home except under a pre-approved business continuity arrangement. Recorded lines and communications surveillance requirements apply in all cases. Quant Analysts may work remotely when using approved tooling against PricingSvc and DataLake, but order entry stays on the desk.

Operations: Wire Room Specialists, Payments Specialists, and Settlements Specialists must work on-site for WireRoom and PaymentsGateway release activity. Reconciliation Analysts may work remotely on ReconLegacy and GLCore review, provided breaks are posted in #recon as usual.

Compliance: AML and KYC staff may work remotely on AMLMonitor, FraudScore, SanctionsScreen, and SARFiling alerts, with the same turnaround expectations as in the office. Ownership of KYCPipeline moves from Operations to Compliance on 2026-10-06, and from that date Compliance sets remote access standards for pipeline reviewers. Until then, Operations retains that responsibility. SAR drafts and supporting evidence must stay inside DocVault.

Wealth Management and Lending: Advisors, Relationship Managers, and Loan Officers may work remotely using ClientHub, PortfolioMgr, and LoanOrigination through AuthSSO. Client calls must be taken in a private space where conversations cannot be overheard. Client details must never be recorded in personal notes or messaging apps.

M&A Advisory: Deal teams may work remotely, but anyone on Project Falcon or any other wall-crossed deal must work in a private space and may not discuss deal matters in shared areas or with household members. Deal discussions stay in the designated private channels and approved data rooms only.

Risk and Technology: Risk staff may work remotely on RiskEngine and ReportingBI. Engineers and Site Reliability Engineers may work remotely with production access granted just in time and logged. Changes to critical systems such as MarketDataFeed, PricingSvc, PositionStore, and AuthSSO follow the standard change process regardless of location.

Availability and Incident Response
Remote employees must be reachable on Slack and phone during agreed working hours. Anyone on call must be able to join an incident bridge within 15 minutes and have stable connectivity and a backup connection option. Post incident updates in #incidents and Technology issues in #it-ops. If your laptop is lost or stolen, or you suspect a security issue, report it to Technology and Compliance immediately.

Overseas and Temporary Locations
Working from outside the United States requires written approval from your department head, Compliance, and Technology in advance. Access from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions is prohibited. Working from a location other than your home for more than five consecutive business days also requires approval.

Equipment and Expenses
Technology issues laptops, headsets, and security keys. Employees are responsible for a reliable home internet connection. Report equipment problems through the IT service desk.

Exceptions, Enforcement, and Review
Exceptions require written approval from the relevant department head and the Chief Operating Officer. Violations may result in loss of remote privileges and disciplinary action. Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer, will review this policy with Linda Brandt, Chief Operating Officer, and Sam Okafor, Director of Engineering, at least annually and after any significant security or regulatory event.
